sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 6.6% a year, from $37.8 billion in FY2017 to $67.4 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F196].
Growth was slow until FY2022, then stepped up: revenue rose 17.7% in FY2023 and 17.3% in FY2026 [D280][D421].
The FY2023 step came primarily from revenue contributions from the Cerner acquisition, which accounted for $5.9 billion of revenue that year [P48][S61].
In FY2026, cloud infrastructure supplied 84% of constant currency cloud growth, and its revenue rose 76.9% to $18.1 billion [P17][D644][S92].
In FY2022 operating margin fell 11.8pp to 25.7%, as litigation related charges lifted operating expenses [D246][F30][P58].
Cloud Infrastructure contributed 13.7pp of the 17.3% FY2026 growth and now makes up 26.9% of revenue [D645][D421][D643].
Cloud Applications added 2.8pp, while Software License fell 8.9% and subtracted 0.8pp [D668][D681][D682].
The filing attributes the $9.3 billion rise in cloud and software revenues to customers buying applications and infrastructure technologies and renewing cloud contracts [P17][P20].
Revenue growth minus operating-cost growth was -0.3pp in FY2026, and incremental operating margin was 29.4% against 52.4% in FY2025 [D443][D442][D395].
Diluted EPS compounded at 11.2% against 6.7% for net income, as diluted shares fell from 4,217m in FY2017 to 2,914m in FY2026 [F201][F199][X136][X145].
Operating margin of 30.6% in FY2026 sits below the 32.2% window median and the 37.6% high, but above the 25.7% low [F34][D788][D787][D786].
The FY2026 bridge shows R&D adding 1.9pp and all other lines subtracting 2.1pp, for a net change of -0.2pp [D444][D445][D433].
Higher infrastructure expenses to support cloud infrastructure lowered the cloud and software margin, with cloud and software expenses up $6.0 billion [P16][P19].
The cost of building capacity is now visible in margin, and R&D leverage offset only part of it [D444][D445].
Operating cash flow rose 53.6% to $32.0 billion in FY2026, helped by $4.6 billion of customer prepayments with a significant financing component [D426][F84][P6].
Capex of $55.7 billion was 82.6% of revenue and 7.30x depreciation and amortization [F94][D404][D410].
Free cash flow was -$23.7 billion, a -35.2% margin against a 26.0% window median [F104][D405][D794].
Free cash flow was -1.39x net income against a 1.06x window median, using FY2026 net income taken from the proxy statement [D409][D800][F44].
Net debt reached $97.6 billion, up from $81.4 billion, and at 145.0% of revenue ranks in the 0th percentile of six software peers [D414][D367][D415][D815].
Total debt rose 39.9% to $129.5 billion, as the company issued $42.7 billion of senior notes net of costs during FY2026 [D440][D413][P7].
Cash and investments of $31.9 billion cover 1.3 years of the FY2026 free cash flow burn [D412][D419].
Buybacks fell to $95 million against $5.8 billion of dividends, and diluted shares still rose 1.7% [X155][X165][D438].
Runway is short: cash and investments cover 1.3 years of burn, against 28.4 years in FY2025, and the burn was funded by debt [R1][D419][D372][P4].
Free cash flow ran at -0.03x net income in FY2025 and -1.39x in FY2026, against a 1.90x peer median, as capex rose $34.4 billion [R2][D362][D409][D818][P5].
Leverage is rising: debt grew 39.9% in FY2026, and interest expense reached $4.6 billion from $3.6 billion on higher borrowings [R4][D413][X92][X91][P10].
Commitments are not on the balance sheet: $260 billion of additional lease commitments, substantially all for data centers, start between FY2027 and FY2029 [P1].
Data check: FY2026 net income of $17.0 billion in the table is proxy-sourced and rounded, and differs from the 10-K figure of $17.1 billion [R5][F44][X20].
Free cash flow margin rising above FY2026's -35.2% would confirm that the capex burden is peaking; a lower reading would reverse that view [D405][D792], in the FY2027 10-K.
Cloud Infrastructure revenue growth below FY2026's 76.9% while capex stays at 82.6% of revenue would weaken the case for the spending [D644][D404], in the FY2027 10-K.
A Cloud and Software segment margin below FY2026's 58.9% would show infrastructure costs still compressing margin [D761], in the FY2027 10-K.
